claims.text: The initial as-cast refractory HEA is single-phase BCC.
The initial alloy has a uniform elemental distribution.
The initial alloy has minimal preexisting chemical short-range order.
Controlled annealing can increase chemical short-range order in the refractory HEA.
Annealing can increase short-range order while retaining the same overall BCC phase structure.
Chemical short-range order increases local lattice distortion.
Localized lattice distortions act as pinning sites for dislocations.
Pinning by localized lattice distortions reduces dislocation mobility.
Short-range-order-induced lattice distortions modify the alloy's elastic response.
Increasing short-range order enhances yield strength relative to the disordered as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples with greater short-range order will have higher yield strength than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples with greater short-range order will exhibit a shifted elastic-modulus response relative to the as-cast baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase BCC refractory HEAs below temperatures that cause significant phase transformations or recrystallization.
HRTEM or APT can quantify the degree of chemical short-range order in the samples.
X-ray diffraction peak broadening or neutron scattering can characterize the proposed lattice distortion.

contradictions.description: The conditions require the samples to have identical microstructure aside from short-range order, while the proposed mediator requires the ordered sample also to differ in local lattice distortion. If lattice distortion is treated as a microstructural feature, both statements cannot hold literally.
